name: Pendred Syndrome

criteria.description: Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss, often congenital or early childhood onset
Presence of thyroid goiter, typically developing in late childhood or adolescence
Abnormal perchlorate discharge test indicating impaired iodide organification
Identification of biallelic pathogenic mutations in the SLC26A4 gene
Imaging evidence of enlarged vestibular aqueduct or Mondini malformation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss plus thyroid goiter, supported by genetic testing or imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for SLC26A4 mutations is confirmatory; perchlorate discharge test may be used when genetic testing is unavailable.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically congenital or early childhood onset, progressive
Usually develops in late childhood or adolescence

common.notes: Incomplete cochlear development seen on imaging

occasional.notes: Transient episodes related to inner ear dysfunction

rare.symptomName: Overt hypothyroidism symptoms (e.g. cold intolerance, weight gain)
Sensorineural hearing loss progression to profound deafness
rare.notes: Occurs in a minority of cases

laboratory: Abnormal perchlorate discharge test indicating defective iodide organification
Possible mild hypothyroidism with elevated TSH
imaging: Enlarged vestibular aqueduct on temporal bone CT or MRI
genetic: Biallelic pathogenic mutations in SLC26A4 gene
other: Family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Hearing loss with enlarged vestibular aqueduct but no thyroid abnormalities
Absence of goiter or thyroid dysfunction
Sensorineural hearing loss with diabetes mellitus and optic atrophy

redFlags: Sudden onset of vertigo or imbalance
references: Pendred V. Deaf-mutism and goitre. Lancet. 1896;1:532-534.
Everett LA, Glaser B, Beck JC, et al. Pendred syndrome is caused by mutations in a putative sulphate transporter gene (PDS). Nat Genet. 1997;17(4):411-422.
Mazzoli M, Castorina P, Bortolozzi M, et al. Pendred syndrome: clinical, molecular, and functional studies. J Med Genet. 2001;38(10):695-701.
